solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: At war camp, little child that grows up

parts.note: a stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child living in a wartime prison camp, growing up there.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is the cave formation that rises from the floor, building upward as mineral deposits accumulate.

clue.text: Tears boldly at first into emergency!

indicators.note: into means the picked letter goes inside the emergency signal

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal used in an emergency

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word boldly

explanation.surface: Someone bursting boldly into tears, treating it as a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobs are the noisy weeping that comes with tears, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Pull a vehicle back in races against time

indicators.note: against means the next piece is placed up against, beside, the rest

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the famous motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: back means the word for the vehicle is read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car being pulled back in a race against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, the Isle of Man motorcycle races, is the standard crossword reading of 'races'; 'in' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, as a magnet pulls iron.

clue.text: Analysed lung, damaged many years ago

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of the two words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical report: the analysed lung turned out to be damaged long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ANALYSED LUNG uses all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots phrase from the Burns song means 'old long since', times long past.

clue.text: Managed to get into party, but accepted second-best

parts.note: to make the team or the final is to manage to get into it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone failed to reach the party they wanted and settled for a lesser one.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to cope with whatever is available, settling for less than the ideal.

clue.text: Frustrating crossing a river? In no hurry

indicators.note: crossing means the first word stretches across, enclosing, the other pieces

parts.note: trying means irritating or frustrating

explanation.surface: A slow, frustrating river crossing for someone who isn't hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarrying means lingering or dawdling, staying longer than needed.

clue.text: Small dog's large slice of cake

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a lab, short for Labrador, is a breed of dog; the 's means 'has'

explanation.surface: The dog has got hold of a hefty piece of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slab is a thick flat piece, as of cake or chocolate.

clue.text: Criminal foe will, when going wild

indicators.note: going wild signals that the letters run riot and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An enemy's intentions run out of control and turn criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowlife is a disreputable person, typically a petty crook.

clue.text: A single trite quotation, under plain cover, all Jane's Sir Walter would read?

definitions.text: all Jane's Sir Walter would read?

indicators.note: under together with cover says these pieces sit beneath a covering
cover with under means the plain word wraps around the inner pieces

parts.note: bare means plain, unadorned
one means a single thing
a tag is a hackneyed quotation or saying

explanation.surface: A cliché quoted in a plain-wrapped book, the only reading Austen's Sir Walter enjoys.
explanation.walkthrough: In Jane Austen's Persuasion, Sir Walter Elliot reads nothing but the Baronetage, the register of baronets, where his own entry delights him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baronetage is the reference book listing baronets and their families, Sir Walter Elliot's only reading in Persuasion.

clue.text: British tolerated corrupt game

indicators.note: corrupt signals that the letters are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Britain is accused of putting up with a crooked sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Battledore and shuttlecock was an old game, ancestor of badminton.

clue.text: One spouted, always inhibiting wife

indicators.note: inhibiting means holding in, so the word for always encloses the letter

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone who always talked over his wife, keeping her quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug with a spout, so it is one fitted with a spout.

clue.text: As far as one can see, account is on the level

parts.words: As far as one can see
parts.note: the horizon is the limit of one's view
a tally is a running account or record

explanation.surface: An honest bookkeeper insists the accounts are straight, as far as can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying horizontally means lying flat, level with the ground; 'on the level' here means flat, not honest.

clue.text: Morning rush hour perhaps not a matter for debate

definitions.meaning: read literally, an ... is movement early in the day, like commuter traffic
in the UK Parliament, an ... is one tabled by MPs that is almost never actually debated

explanation.surface: Morning traffic jams, it is claimed, are not worth arguing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Early day motions are formal House of Commons motions that record opinions but are rarely given time for debate.

clue.text: Employment system brought an end to trading

definitions.meaning: a workplace where all workers must belong to a particular trade union
read as a verb phrase, a business that shut up its store stopped trading

explanation.surface: A new workplace arrangement killed off the business.
explanation.definitionFit: A union-only workplace is the employment arrangement; literally, the words describe a store that was shut down.

clue.text: Fine writing, if short; some makes the long list

parts.note: lit is the short form of literature, fine writing
any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: A good short story might just make it onto the longlist for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long, tedious recital or catalogue, from the series of prayers of that name.

clue.text: Poor country deserted by last fellow

indicators.note: deserted by its last letter means the country's name loses its final letter

parts.note: India is a country
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A poor nation is abandoned by its final citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent means needy, lacking the means to live.

clue.text: Gentle persuasion something that's comfortable for prisoner in hearing?

indicators.note: in hearing signals that the phrase is said out loud and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: a comfortable room for an inmate would be a soft cell

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene: gentle coaxing at a hearing to make a prisoner comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hearing' looks like a court hearing, but it signals that SOFT CELL is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sell is a low-pressure sales approach, coaxing rather than pushing.

clue.text: Still sound irritated by attempt

parts.note: to snap is to speak sharply, sounding irritated
a shot is an attempt, as in 'have a shot'

explanation.surface: Someone sounds annoyed at the latest try, yet keeps going.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, and a snapshot is a quickly taken photo.

clue.text: Warning to bring gold forward: there will be lots here

indicators.note: bring with forward says the named piece is moved
forward with bring sends the gold symbol towards the front of the word

parts.note: a caution is a warning
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A cautionary note about bringing gold to a place where plenty awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring ... forward' moves AU from the second and third places of CAUTION to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction, goods are sold in numbered lots, so it is a place full of lots.

clue.text: Maybe wolf this popular, a pet

parts.note: hot means popular, in demand
a dog is a pet

explanation.surface: A wolf, perhaps, becomes a popular pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wolf' looks like the animal, a cousin of the pet dog, but it is the verb: to gobble food.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a bun is the kind of snack one might wolf down quickly.

clue.text: Sundew and red rose rat's eaten away

indicators.note: eaten away means the outer letters of the phrase are gnawed off, leaving what lies within

explanation.surface: A gardener's lament: the sundew and a red rose have been gnawed by a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: With the outer R and TS eaten away, the letters running through RED ROSE RAT'S remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Drosera is the botanical genus of carnivorous plants commonly called sundews.

clue.text: Massage a digit, mostly in irregular rhythm

parts.note: to rub is to massage

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot

explanation.surface: A massage of one toe, done with an uneven beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato in music is the expressive speeding up and slowing down of tempo, so the rhythm is not strict.

clue.text: Open to fraud, ruin some textual analysis

indicators.note: open to means the word for ruin opens up to let the fraud in

parts.note: destruction is ruin
a con is a fraud or swindle

explanation.surface: A scheme vulnerable to swindlers, risking financial ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Deconstruction is Derrida's method of critical reading, a kind of analysis of texts.

clue.text: Cook welcomes a brawl

indicators.note: welcomes means the cooking word takes in the letter as a guest

parts.note: to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A chef greets someone who turns up looking for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or scuffle.

clue.text: One visiting woman's eldest son perhaps

indicators.note: visiting means one piece calls in on, and goes inside, the other

parts.note: her means the woman's, belonging to her
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone calls at a lady's house: her eldest son, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Under primogeniture the eldest son is the one who inherits, an example of the successor to an estate.

clue.text: Throw off course, breaking rule that's applied to cycles

parts.note: to derail is to throw off course

indicators.note: breaking means the word is broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone rule-breaking enough to knock a cyclist off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A derailleur is the gear-changing mechanism fitted to bicycles.

clue.text: A speculative kick?

parts.note: the word for a drop kick of the ball also means a speculative bet

explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a punt is a kick of the dropped ball; in British slang a punt is also a gamble, so it is a speculative kick.

clue.text: Drink fuddled old boy, joining wrong army

indicators.note: fuddled means confused, so these letters are muddled up
wrong signals the letters are put in the wrong order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken old soldier joins the wrong army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuddled' makes BLOODY from OLD BOY; 'wrong' makes MARY from ARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice.
